title: Visceral hypersensitivity
objective: Explain visceral hypersensitivity and the role of silent nociceptors, using colitis as a model.

steps.title: When the gut turns up its volume
steps.body: **[[visceral hypersensitivity]]** is heightened sensation from the viscera — normal filling now feels painful. Inflammation (e.g. **[[colitis]]**) sensitizes gut afferents and can **recruit [[silent nociceptor|silent nociceptors]]**: afferents that don't respond to mechanical stimuli at baseline but 'wake up' and start firing once inflamed.

options: Mechanically insensitive at rest, but responsive once inflamed
An afferent whose firing never reaches conscious sensation at all
A nociceptor that fires steadily on its own without any stimulus
A touch fiber that switches to carrying pain after an injury
steps.explanation: Silent (or 'sleeping') nociceptors don't respond to normal mechanical stimuli until inflammation sensitizes them — then they add to the barrage, a key contributor to visceral hypersensitivity.

variants.setup: After colon inflammation, more afferents respond to distension than before.
options: The existing afferents began conducting more quickly
New afferents sprouted in from the spinal cord
variants.reveal: Inflammation wakes silent nociceptors, adding to the active population.

steps.setup: In a colitis model, a mouse shows pain behavior to colon distension that a healthy mouse ignores.
options: Peripheral sensitization, silent nociceptors, and central sensitization
Only central sensitization; the gut afferents themselves are unchanged
Only peripheral sensitization at the endings, with no central change
Faster conduction velocity in the existing colon afferents
steps.reveal: Visceral hypersensitivity is multi-level: sensitized endings, newly-recruited silent nociceptors, and raised dorsal-horn gain together make normal filling feel painful. This is the model the lab's tools can dissect.

variants.prompt: Painful responses to normal distension after colitis reflect…
options: Peripheral + central sensitization and silent-nociceptor recruitment
Only sensitized endings, with no change in the dorsal horn
Only faster conduction in the existing afferents, nothing more
variants.explanation: Multiple sensitization mechanisms combine to produce visceral hypersensitivity.

sources.note: Gut enterochromaffin cells drive visceral pain and anxiety.
